questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं :
कथन-I : नेपाल अतीत में एक हिन्दू राज्य था, फिर आधुनिक काल में यहाँ कई सालों तक संवैधानिक राजतंत्र रहा ।
कथन-II : 2006 में यहाँ देशव्यापी लोकतंत्र समर्थक प्रदर्शन हुए । संघर्षरत लोकतंत्र समर्थक शक्तियों ने अपनी पहली बड़ी जीत तब हासिल की जब राजा ने बाध्य होकर संसद को बहाल किया ।
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : Nepal was a Hindu Kingdom in the past and then a constitutional monarchy in the modern period for many years.
Statement-II : The struggling pro-democracy forces achieved their first major victory in 2006 when the king was forced to restore the House of representatives.

options.A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं ।
options.B: कथन I और कथन II दोनों असत्य हैं ।
options.C: कथन I सत्य है, लेकिन कथन II असत्य है ।
options.D: कथन I असत्य है, लेकिन कथन II सत्य है ।

options_english.A: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
options_english.B: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options_english.C: Statement-I is true, but Statement-II is false.
options_english.D: Statement-I is false, but Statement-II is true.

questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Statement-I is true because Nepal was indeed a Hindu Kingdom historically and later became a constitutional monarchy for several decades. Statement-II is also true because in 2006, widespread pro-democracy protests compelled King Gyanendra to restore the dissolved parliament, marking the first major victory for democratic forces in Nepal. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because they wrongly suggest one or both statements are false.
questions.solution_hindi: दोनों कथन सही हैं। कथन-I सत्य है क्योंकि नेपाल ऐतिहासिक रूप से एक हिन्दू राज्य था और बाद में कई दशकों तक संवैधानिक राजतंत्र रहा। कथन-II भी सत्य है क्योंकि 2006 में व्यापक लोकतंत्र समर्थक प्रदर्शनों के कारण राजा ज्ञानेंद्र को भंग संसद को बहाल करना पड़ा, जो लोकतांत्रिक शक्तियों की पहली बड़ी जीत थी।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस घटना के कारण शीतयुद्ध के बाद दक्षिण एशियाई क्षेत्र ने अचानक पूरे विश्व का ध्यान आकर्षित किया ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following events made the South Asian region a sudden focus of global attention after the cold war period ?

options.A: 1971 का बांग्लादेश युद्ध
options.C: भारत और पाकिस्तान दोनों का परमाणु शक्ति बनना
options.D: भारत और पाकिस्तान के बीच कारगिल संघर्ष

options_english.C: India and Pakistan both became nuclear power
options_english.D: Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan

questions.solution: Option C is correct. After the Cold War, when both India and Pakistan conducted nuclear tests in 1998, the South Asian region suddenly became a focus of global attention because the world feared a nuclear arms race between two hostile neighbours. The 1971 Bangladesh War (A) and Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict (B) were significant but regional events. The Kargil conflict (D) came after the nuclear tests and was itself a consequence of the heightened tensions.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। शीतयुद्ध के बाद 1998 में भारत और पाकिस्तान दोनों ने परमाणु परीक्षण किए, जिससे दक्षिण एशिया अचानक विश्व का ध्यान केंद्र बन गया क्योंकि दुनिया को दो शत्रु पड़ोसियों के बीच परमाणु हथियारों की होड़ का डर था।

questions.text: कॉलम A में दिए गए पदों का कॉलम B के साथ सही मिलान कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए कूटों से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Match the terms given in Column-'A' correctly with Column-'B' and choose the correct answer from the codes given below :

options.A: I-iii, II-i, III-iv, IV-ii
options.D: I-ii, II-iv, III-iii, IV-i

questions.solution: Option C is correct: Human Rights Watch (I) is an international NGO (iv); the International Monetary Fund (II) is an international organisation that oversees financial institutions (iii); the World Health Organisation (III) is an agency of the United Nations (ii); and the General Assembly (IV) is an organ of the United Nations (i). The other options mix up the matches incorrectly.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है: ह्यूमन राइट्स वॉच एक अंतर्राष्ट्रीय स्वयंसेवी संस्था है; IMF एक अंतर्राष्ट्रीय वित्तीय संस्था है; WHO संयुक्त राष्ट्र की एजेंसी है; और आम सभा संयुक्त राष्ट्र का एक अंग है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित को उनके गठन के कालक्रम अनुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
I. विश्व व्यापार संगठन
II. विश्व बैंक
III. अंतर्राष्ट्रीय परमाणु ऊर्जा एजेंसी
IV. संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ
सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their formation :
I. The World Trade Organisation
II. World Bank
III. The International Atomic Energy Agency
IV. United Nations Organisation
Choose the correct option :

options.A: I, II, III, IV
options.D: III, I, II, IV

questions.solution: Option B is correct. The World Bank was established in 1944, the United Nations Organisation in 1945, the International Atomic Energy Agency in 1957, and the World Trade Organisation in 1995. So the correct chronological order is II (World Bank, 1944), IV (UNO, 1945), III (IAEA, 1957), I (WTO, 1995). The other options present incorrect sequences.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। विश्व बैंक 1944 में, संयुक्त राष्ट्र 1945 में, IAEA 1957 में और WTO 1995 में स्थापित हुए। इसलिए सही क्रम II, IV, III, I है।

questions.text: आर्थिक रूप से कमज़ोर लोगों पर वैश्वीकरण के नकारात्मक प्रभावों को कम करने के लिए अपनाए गए संस्थागत सुरक्षा उपायों को निम्नलिखित में से क्या कहा जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Institutional safeguards to minimize the negative effects of globalization on those who are economically weak are known as _______.

options.A: कल्याणकारी उपाय
options.D: स्वैच्छिक सेवाएँ

questions.solution: Option B is correct. Social safety nets are institutional safeguards put in place by governments and international organisations to protect economically vulnerable people from the harmful effects of globalization, such as unemployment and poverty. Welfare measures (A) is a broader term. Economic liberalization (C) is itself a cause of negative effects. Voluntary services (D) are not institutional safeguards.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। सामाजिक सुरक्षा जाल वे संस्थागत उपाय हैं जो सरकारें वैश्वीकरण के नकारात्मक प्रभावों से आर्थिक रूप से कमज़ोर लोगों की रक्षा के लिए लागू करती हैं।
questions.topic: Impact of Globalisation and Social Safety Nets

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न में दो कथनों को क्रमशः अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है । उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए ।
अभिकथन (A) : विश्व भर में बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियों के प्रवेश और बढ़ती भूमिका से सरकारों की स्वयं निर्णय लेने की क्षमता में कमी आई है ।
कारण (R) : राज्य अपने अनिवार्य कार्यों को निरन्तर पूरा कर रहे हैं और बहुत सोच-समझकर अपने कदम उन्हीं दायरों से बाहर खींच रहे हैं जहाँ से वे चाहते हैं ।
questions.text_english:
In the following question, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option as answer.
Assertion (A) : The entry and the increased role of multinational companies all over the world leads to a reduction in the capacity of governments to take decisions on their own.
Reason (R) : The state continues to discharge its essential functions and consciously withdraws from certain domains from which it wishes to.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) गलत है ।

options_english.A: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct, but the Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: The Assertion (A) is incorrect, but the Reason (R) is correct.
options_english.D: The Assertion (A) is correct, but the Reason (R) is incorrect.

questions.solution: Option B is correct. The Assertion is true because the growing role of MNCs does reduce the autonomous decision-making capacity of governments, as these companies exert enormous economic pressure. The Reason is also true because states do continue to perform essential functions and do withdraw consciously from certain domains. However, the Reason does not explain why MNCs reduce state autonomy; it actually presents a separate phenomenon. Hence both are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। अभिकथन सत्य है क्योंकि MNC की बढ़ती भूमिका सरकारों की स्वायत्त निर्णय क्षमता कम करती है। कारण भी सत्य है लेकिन वह अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित कथनों में से कौन सा कथन नीति आयोग का उद्देश्य नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one among the following statements is not the objective of NITI Aayog ?

options.A: भारत की विकास प्रक्रिया के लिए एक महत्त्वपूर्ण दिशात्मक और रणनीतिक नीति प्रदान करना ।
options.B: केंद्रीय व राज्य स्तर पर सरकार के लिए थिंक टैंक के रूप में कार्य करना ।
options.C: विकास कार्यक्रमों के क्रियान्वयन के लिए धन की व्यवस्था करना ।
options.D: नीतियों के धीमे और मंद कार्यान्वयन को समाप्त करने का प्रयास करना ।

options_english.A: Provide a critical directional and strategic input to the development process of India.
options_english.B: Serve as a think tank of the government both at the centre and state level.
options_english.C: Arrange funds for the implementation of developmental programs.
options_english.D: Seek to put an end to the slow and tardy implementation of the policies.

questions.solution: Option C is correct because arranging funds for the implementation of developmental programs is NOT an objective of NITI Aayog. NITI Aayog is a policy think tank and advisory body; the actual allocation and disbursement of funds is the function of the Finance Commission and the Finance Ministry. Options A, B, and D are all genuine objectives of NITI Aayog.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है क्योंकि विकास कार्यक्रमों के लिए धन की व्यवस्था करना नीति आयोग का उद्देश्य नहीं है। नीति आयोग एक नीति-निर्माण थिंक टैंक है, न कि वित्त आवंटित करने वाली संस्था।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन नियोजन की वामपंथी विचारधारा के बारे में सही है ?
questions.text_english: Which statement among the following is correct about the planning ideology of left wing ?

options.A: वामपंथी एक मुक्त बाजार अर्थव्यवस्था का समर्थन करते हैं ।
options.B: वे गरीब लोगों के लाभ के लिए निर्मित सरकारी नीतियों का समर्थन करते हैं ।
options.C: वे अर्थव्यवस्था में सरकार का अनावश्यक हस्तक्षेप नहीं चाहते हैं ।
options.D: वे प्रगतिशील नीतियों की वकालत करते हैं ।

options_english.A: The Left supports a free-market economy.
options_english.B: They support government policies which are for the benefit of poor sections.
options_english.C: They do not want unnecessary intervention of government in the economy.

questions.solution: Option B is correct. The left-wing ideology in planning believes in state intervention to protect the poor and marginalised sections of society, and therefore supports government policies that benefit the economically weaker classes. Option A is incorrect as free-market economy is a right-wing idea. Option C is also associated with right-wing thinking. Option D is partially correct but too vague to be the best answer.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। वामपंथी विचारधारा में यह माना जाता है कि सरकार को गरीब और हाशिये पर रहने वाले लोगों की रक्षा के लिए नीतियाँ बनानी चाहिए। मुक्त बाजार और कम सरकारी हस्तक्षेप दक्षिणपंथी विचार हैं।

questions.text: 1969 में कांग्रेस के विभाजन के मुख्य कारण की पहचान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Identify the main reason for the split in Congress Party in 1969.

options.A: कांग्रेस पार्टी की विचारधारा में बदलाव आना ।
options.C: विपक्षी दलों के बीच वैचारिक मतभेद
options.D: विपक्षी दलों का एक साथ आना

options_english.A: Change in the ideology of Congress Party
options_english.C: Difference of opinion among the opposition parties

questions.solution: Option B is correct. The main reason for the split in the Congress Party in 1969 was the dominance of the Congress Syndicate, a group of powerful senior leaders who tried to control Indira Gandhi and impose their candidate for the President's election. Indira Gandhi challenged their authority by supporting V.V. Giri against the official Congress candidate, leading to the party splitting into Congress (O) and Congress (R). Options C and D relate to opposition parties and are therefore incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। 1969 में कांग्रेस विभाजन का मुख्य कारण कांग्रेस सिंडिकेट का प्रभुत्व था जो इंदिरा गांधी को नियंत्रित करने का प्रयास कर रहा था। इंदिरा गांधी ने सिंडिकेट के उम्मीदवार के खिलाफ वी.वी. गिरी का समर्थन किया, जिससे पार्टी विभाजित हो गई।

questions.text: गलत जोड़ों को पहचानिए और लिखिए :
questions.text_english: Identify and choose the incorrect pair :

options.A: लाल बहादुर शास्त्री – जय जवान जय किसान
options.C: सिंडिकेट – इन्दिरा गांधी के विरुद्ध विपक्ष के शक्तिशाली नेताओं का समूह
options.D: महागठबंधन – सभी गैर-कांग्रेसी दलों का गठन

options_english.A: Lal Bahadur Shastri – Jai Jawan Jai Kisan
options_english.C: Syndicate – A group of powerful opposition leaders against Indira Gandhi
options_english.D: Grand Alliance – Formed by all Non-Congress Parties

questions.solution: Option C is the incorrect pair. The Syndicate was not a group of opposition leaders; it was a group of powerful senior leaders WITHIN the Congress Party who opposed Indira Gandhi's decisions. Leaders like K. Kamaraj, S. Nijalingappa and others formed this internal pressure group. Option A is correct (Shastri gave the Jai Jawan Jai Kisan slogan), Option B is correct (Indira Gandhi's Garibi Hatao campaign), and Option D is correct about the Grand Alliance.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C गलत जोड़ा है। सिंडिकेट विपक्षी दलों का नहीं बल्कि कांग्रेस के भीतर के वरिष्ठ नेताओं का समूह था जो इंदिरा गांधी का विरोध करते थे।

questions.text: 2019 के भाजपा नेतृत्व वाले गठबंधन को निम्नलिखित में से किस नाम से जाना जाता है ?
questions.text_english: BJP led alliance of 2019 is known as :

options.A: संयुक्त प्रगतिशील गठबन्धन
options.D: लोकतांत्रिक गठबंधन

questions.solution: Option C is correct. The BJP-led alliance is known as the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), which won a landslide victory in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections under the leadership of Narendra Modi. The United Progressive Alliance (A) is led by the Congress party. The United Front (B) was a coalition of the 1990s. Democratic Coalition (D) is not a real alliance name.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है। भाजपा नेतृत्व वाले गठबंधन को राष्ट्रीय लोकतान्त्रिक गठबन्धन (NDA) कहा जाता है। संयुक्त प्रगतिशील गठबन्धन कांग्रेस के नेतृत्व में था।

questions.text: 1999 के लोकसभा चुनावों के बाद किसने केन्द्रीय सरकार का नेतृत्व किया था ?
questions.text_english: Who led the Central Government after the 1999 Lok Sabha Elections ?

options.A: पी.वी. नरसिम्हा राव
options.D: एच.डी. देवगौड़ा

questions.solution: Option B is correct. After the 1999 Lok Sabha elections, Atal Bihari Vajpayee led the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government as Prime Minister. P.V. Narasimha Rao (A) was PM from 1991-1996. H.D. Deve Gowda (D) led the United Front government in 1996-97. Manmohan Singh (C) became PM in 2004 after the UPA victory.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। 1999 के लोकसभा चुनावों के बाद अटल बिहारी वाजपेयी के नेतृत्व में NDA सरकार बनी। मनमोहन सिंह 2004 में प्रधानमंत्री बने थे।

questions.text: क्या शॉक थेरैपी को सोवियत संघ के विघटन के बाद सत्तावादी समाजवादी व्यवस्था से उदारवादी लोकतान्त्रिक पूँजीवादी व्यवस्था की तरफ संक्रमण का सबसे बेहतर तरीका कहा जा सकता है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Can Shock Therapy be called the best way to make transition from authoritarian socialist system to liberal capitalist system after the disintegration of Soviet Union ? Explain.

key_points: Shock Therapy was a rapid, painful transition model imposed on post-Soviet states
It led to collapse of economies, widespread poverty, and loss of state assets
It cannot be called the best method because it caused more harm than good

questions.solution: Shock Therapy cannot be called the best way to make this transition. It was a rapid, externally imposed model of economic transformation recommended by the World Bank and the IMF for the post-Soviet states of Russia and Eastern Europe. It involved sudden privatisation, removal of state controls, and opening up of economies to foreign capital. However, the results were disastrous: Russia's GDP fell drastically, industries collapsed, unemployment rose sharply, and poverty increased massively. The state-owned assets were sold at throwaway prices to a handful of oligarchs. Social services deteriorated rapidly and large sections of the population fell into poverty. A more gradual, state-guided transition, as seen in China, would have been far more effective.
questions.solution_hindi: शॉक थेरैपी संक्रमण का सबसे बेहतर तरीका नहीं कहा जा सकता। यह एक तीव्र, बाहरी रूप से थोपी गई आर्थिक परिवर्तन की नीति थी जिसे विश्व बैंक और IMF ने सुझाया था। इससे रूस और पूर्वी यूरोप में GDP में भारी गिरावट, बेरोजगारी में वृद्धि और व्यापक गरीबी फैली। चीन का क्रमिक परिवर्तन इससे बेहतर मॉडल था।

questions.text: वैश्वीकरण के किन्हीं दो प्रमुख कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any two major causes of globalization.

key_points: Technological advancement, especially in communication and transport
Liberalisation of trade and investment policies by governments worldwide

questions.solution: The two major causes of globalization are: First, technological advancement, particularly in communication and information technology. The invention of the internet, mobile telephony, and faster modes of transport like containerised shipping have dramatically reduced the cost and time required to move goods, services, capital, and ideas across borders. Second, the deliberate liberalisation of trade and investment policies by national governments, often encouraged by international institutions like the WTO and IMF. Countries lowered tariff barriers, opened up their markets to foreign investment, and adopted free-trade agreements, enabling businesses to operate on a global scale.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्वीकरण के दो प्रमुख कारण हैं: पहला, प्रौद्योगिकी में प्रगति, विशेष रूप से इंटरनेट और संचार प्रौद्योगिकी का विकास जिसने वस्तुओं, सेवाओं और विचारों के प्रवाह को सरल बनाया। दूसरा, विश्व भर में सरकारों द्वारा व्यापार और निवेश नीतियों का उदारीकरण, जिसमें WTO जैसी संस्थाओं की भूमिका रही।

questions.text: स्वतंत्रता के बाद प्राप्त हुए उन दो लक्ष्यों की व्याख्या कीजिए जिन पर राष्ट्रीय आन्दोलन के दौरान व्यापक सहमति थी ।
questions.text_english: Explain the two commonly agreed upon goals of the national movement which were achieved after independence.

key_points: Establishment of a democratic system of governance
Development and social-economic transformation for all citizens

questions.solution: Two goals broadly agreed upon during the national movement and achieved after independence were: First, the establishment of a democratic form of government. There was near-universal consensus among national leaders that independent India would be governed as a democracy where citizens would elect their representatives and enjoy fundamental rights. This was realised through the Constitution of 1950. Second, the goal of development and social transformation — ensuring economic growth, reducing poverty and inequality, and providing education and health services to all citizens. The Five-Year Plans were launched to achieve planned economic development and improve the standard of living of ordinary Indians.
questions.solution_hindi: राष्ट्रीय आन्दोलन के दौरान जिन दो लक्ष्यों पर व्यापक सहमति थी: पहला, लोकतांत्रिक शासन व्यवस्था की स्थापना — 1950 के संविधान द्वारा प्राप्त किया गया। दूसरा, आर्थिक विकास और सामाजिक परिवर्तन — पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं के माध्यम से गरीबी कम करने और नागरिकों के जीवन-स्तर को सुधारने का लक्ष्य।
questions.topic: Goals of National Movement After Independence

questions.text: विश्व की साझी सम्पदा में सम्मिलित किन्हीं चार अवयवों के नाम लिखिए ।
questions.text_english: Name any four global commons.

key_points: The atmosphere / air
The Antarctic region
The High Seas / international waters
Outer space

questions.solution: Global commons are areas or resources that lie outside the sovereign jurisdiction of any single nation-state and are shared by all of humanity. Four global commons are: (1) The Earth's atmosphere, which all nations share and which requires collective protection from pollution and climate change; (2) Antarctica, which is governed by the Antarctic Treaty and is not owned by any country; (3) The High Seas (international waters), which lie beyond any nation's exclusive economic zone and are open to all; and (4) Outer space, including the moon and other celestial bodies, which are the common heritage of mankind under international law.
questions.solution_hindi: विश्व की साझी सम्पदा वे क्षेत्र या संसाधन हैं जो किसी एक राष्ट्र की संप्रभुता से बाहर हैं। चार उदाहरण: (1) पृथ्वी का वायुमंडल, (2) अंटार्कटिका, (3) खुला समुद्र (हाई सीज), (4) बाह्य अंतरिक्ष।

questions.text: 1967 के चौथे आम चुनावों से पहले के गंभीर आर्थिक संकटों का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: State the severe economic crisis prior to the fourth general elections of 1967.

key_points: Two consecutive droughts causing food crisis and famine-like conditions
Foreign exchange crisis and dependence on US food aid (PL-480)
Devaluation of the rupee in 1966 and rising inflation

questions.solution: Prior to the fourth general elections of 1967, India faced several severe economic crises. Two consecutive years of drought in 1965 and 1966 led to widespread food shortages and near-famine conditions, forcing India to depend heavily on American food aid under the PL-480 programme. The wars with China (1962) and Pakistan (1965) had drained the national treasury and diverted resources from development. India's foreign exchange reserves fell critically low. In 1966, the government was forced to devalue the rupee under pressure from the World Bank and the USA, which caused inflation to rise sharply and led to public discontent.
questions.solution_hindi: 1967 के चुनावों से पहले भारत कई गंभीर आर्थिक संकटों से गुजरा। 1965-66 में दो लगातार सूखों से खाद्य संकट पैदा हुआ। चीन और पाकिस्तान से युद्धों ने खजाने को खाली कर दिया। विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार में भारी कमी आई और 1966 में रुपये का अवमूल्यन करना पड़ा, जिससे महंगाई बढ़ी।

questions.text: "क्षेत्रवाद उतना खतरनाक नहीं है, जितनी सांप्रदायिकता ।" कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: "Regionalism is not as dangerous as communalism." Justify the statement.

key_points: Regionalism demands development and political representation within the constitutional framework
Communalism divides people on religious lines and threatens national unity more fundamentally

questions.solution: Regionalism is not as dangerous as communalism because regional aspirations can be accommodated within the constitutional democratic framework without threatening the country's unity. Regionalism typically demands more autonomy, better development, or a separate state, all of which can be addressed through dialogue, reorganisation of states, or federal arrangements. India has successfully managed regional demands through such means. Communalism, on the other hand, divides society along religious lines and creates an 'us versus them' mentality that has historically led to riots, massacres, and even the partition of the country. Communalism can destabilise entire societies and is far more difficult to resolve peacefully.
questions.solution_hindi: क्षेत्रवाद इसलिए कम खतरनाक है क्योंकि इसकी माँगें संवैधानिक ढाँचे में हल की जा सकती हैं जैसे राज्य पुनर्गठन या स्वायत्तता। सांप्रदायिकता धार्मिक आधार पर समाज को विभाजित करती है, दंगों और हत्याओं को जन्म देती है और देश के विभाजन जैसी त्रासदी का कारण बन सकती है।

questions.text: सोवियत संघ में आर्थिक गतिरोध के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं चार कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any four reasons responsible for the economic stagnation in Soviet Union.

key_points: Over-bureaucratisation and highly centralised command economy stifled innovation
Disproportionate spending on military at the expense of consumer goods and agriculture
Technological backwardness compared to the West, especially in information technology
Corruption and inefficiency within the Communist Party and state institutions

questions.solution: The Soviet Union faced severe economic stagnation due to the following four reasons. First, the Soviet economy was excessively centralised and bureaucratic. All economic decisions were made by the state, which stifled innovation and made the economy inefficient. Enterprises had no incentive to improve quality or reduce costs. Second, there was a massive and disproportionate emphasis on military spending and the arms race with the United States. This drained enormous resources away from consumer goods production and agricultural development, creating shortages for ordinary citizens. Third, the Soviet Union lagged far behind the West in technological development, particularly in the field of information technology and computer science. This technological backwardness made Soviet industries less competitive globally. Fourth, widespread corruption and inefficiency within the Communist Party apparatus and government institutions meant that resources were misallocated, policies were poorly implemented, and the party leadership became increasingly out of touch with the needs of the people and the economy.
questions.solution_hindi: सोवियत संघ में आर्थिक गतिरोध के चार कारण: पहला, अत्यधिक केंद्रीकृत और नौकरशाही अर्थव्यवस्था जिसने नवाचार को दबाया। दूसरा, सैन्य खर्च पर अत्यधिक जोर जिससे उपभोक्ता वस्तुओं और कृषि की अनदेखी हुई। तीसरा, सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी में पश्चिम से पिछड़ापन। चौथा, कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी और सरकारी संस्थानों में व्यापक भ्रष्टाचार।
questions.topic: Reasons for Disintegration of Soviet Union

questions.text:
(a) किस प्रकार दक्षेस (साउथ एशियन एसोशिएशन फॉर रीजनल कोऑपरेशन), दक्षिण एशियाई देशों द्वारा बहुपक्षीय साधनों से आपस में सहयोग करने की दिशा में उठाया गया एक बड़ा कदम है ? आकलन कीजिए ।
अथवा
(b) "लोकतांत्रिक अनुभव के मिश्रित रिकॉर्ड के बावजूद, दक्षिण एशियाई देशों की जनता लोकतंत्र की आकांक्षा में सहभागी है ।" दो उपयुक्त तर्कों से कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) How is the South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC) a major regional initiative by South Asian states to evolve co-operation through multilateral means ? Assess.
OR
(b) "Despite the mixed record of democratic experiences, the people of South Asian countries share the aspiration for democracy." Justify the statement with two suitable arguments.

key_points: SAARC was established in 1985 as a multilateral forum for South Asian cooperation
It promotes trade, cultural exchanges, and collective approaches to common problems
Despite limitations, SAARC represents the aspiration for regional unity
People across South Asia consistently favour democracy in surveys despite military interruptions

questions.solution:
Part (a): SAARC, the South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation, was established in 1985 with seven founding member states: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives. It is a significant regional initiative because it provides a multilateral platform for South Asian nations to cooperate on matters of mutual interest without depending on bilateral channels alone. Through SAARC, member states have worked on agreements related to trade (SAFTA), cultural exchanges, and tackling common challenges like poverty, terrorism, and natural disasters. Despite the limitations caused by the India-Pakistan rivalry, SAARC has kept alive the spirit of regional cooperation and given smaller nations a collective voice. It represents a shared recognition that the problems of South Asia can only be solved through cooperative multilateral action.

Part (b): Despite the mixed democratic record, South Asian people aspire for democracy because, first, every time military or authoritarian rule has been imposed in countries like Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Nepal, the people have consistently risen and demanded the restoration of democracy. The 2006 pro-democracy movement in Nepal and the return to democracy in Bangladesh are clear examples. Second, surveys and opinion polls conducted across South Asian countries consistently show that a large majority of people, regardless of their country's current political system, prefer democracy over any other form of government, indicating a deep-rooted aspiration for democratic governance.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) दक्षेस 1985 में स्थापित दक्षिण एशियाई देशों का एक महत्त्वपूर्ण बहुपक्षीय मंच है। इसके माध्यम से व्यापार (SAFTA), सांस्कृतिक आदान-प्रदान और साझी समस्याओं के समाधान में सहयोग होता है। भारत-पाकिस्तान तनाव के बावजूद यह क्षेत्रीय सहयोग की भावना को जीवित रखता है।
(b) दक्षिण एशिया में लोकतंत्र की आकांक्षा इसलिए है क्योंकि जब भी सैन्य शासन लगा, जनता ने लोकतंत्र की बहाली की माँग की (नेपाल 2006, बांग्लादेश)। सर्वेक्षणों में बहुमत लोकतंत्र को अन्य शासन व्यवस्थाओं से बेहतर मानते हैं।

questions.text: प्रदूषण को रोकने और पर्यावरण को बचाने के लिए भारत सरकार द्वारा उठाए जाने के लिए कोई चार कदम सुझाइये ।
questions.text_english: Suggest any four steps for the Indian Government to take to check the pollution and save the environment.

key_points: Stricter enforcement of pollution control laws and penalties for violators
Promotion of renewable energy sources like solar and wind power
Encouraging public transport and electric vehicles to reduce vehicular pollution
Planting trees on a large scale and protecting existing forests

questions.solution: Four steps the Indian Government should take to check pollution and save the environment are as follows. First, the government should strictly enforce existing environmental laws such as the Environment Protection Act, 1986, and impose heavy penalties on industries and individuals who violate pollution norms. Polluting industries must be held accountable. Second, the government should invest heavily in renewable energy sources like solar, wind, and hydroelectric power to reduce India's dependence on coal and fossil fuels, which are the major causes of air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. Third, the government should promote public transportation systems and provide incentives for the adoption of electric vehicles, as vehicular emissions are a leading cause of air pollution in cities. Fourth, the government must launch large-scale afforestation and reforestation programmes to increase forest cover, as trees absorb carbon dioxide, prevent soil erosion, and maintain ecological balance.
questions.solution_hindi: पर्यावरण बचाने के लिए चार सुझाव: पहला, पर्यावरण कानूनों का सख्त प्रवर्तन और उल्लंघनकर्ताओं पर भारी जुर्माना। दूसरा, सौर और पवन ऊर्जा जैसे नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा स्रोतों में निवेश। तीसरा, सार्वजनिक परिवहन और इलेक्ट्रिक वाहनों को बढ़ावा। चौथा, बड़े पैमाने पर वृक्षारोपण और वन संरक्षण।

questions.text: "एक दलीय प्रभुत्व ने भारतीय लोकतंत्र के मूल सार को प्रभावित नहीं किया ।" किन्हीं दो तर्कों द्वारा कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइये ।
questions.text_english: "One party dominance did not affect the very essence of Indian democracy." Justify the statement with any two arguments.

key_points: Free and fair elections were held regularly despite Congress dominance
Opposition parties existed and functioned freely, and vibrant internal democracy existed within Congress

questions.solution: One-party dominance by the Congress in the first two decades after independence did not undermine the essence of Indian democracy for the following two reasons. First, elections were held regularly, freely, and fairly. The Election Commission functioned as an independent constitutional body, and voters freely exercised their franchise. The Congress did not rig elections or suppress voter turnout. The fact that the Congress could lose seats, as it did in 1952 itself in some constituencies, shows elections were genuinely competitive. Second, opposition parties were allowed to exist, organise, campaign, and contest elections without harassment or suppression. Parties like the CPI, the Socialists, Swatantra Party, and Jana Sangh operated freely. The Congress also had robust internal debate and democratic functioning within the party itself, making it a pluralistic organisation rather than a monolithic authoritarian party.
questions.solution_hindi: एक दलीय प्रभुत्व के बावजूद भारतीय लोकतंत्र के मूल सार पर असर नहीं पड़ा क्योंकि: पहला, चुनाव नियमित, स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष रूप से होते थे और मतदाता स्वतंत्र रूप से मतदान करते थे। दूसरा, विपक्षी दलों को स्वतंत्र रूप से कार्य करने और चुनाव लड़ने का अधिकार था, और कांग्रेस के भीतर भी आंतरिक लोकतंत्र मौजूद था।

questions.text:
(a) भारतीय राष्ट्रीय राजनीति में जयप्रकाश नारायण की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए ।
अथवा
(b) 1977 के लोकसभा चुनावों में जनता पार्टी की विजय के किन्हीं दो कारणों का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Describe the role of Jaya Prakash Narayan in Indian National Politics.
OR
(b) Describe any two reasons for the victory of Janata Party in 1977 Lok Sabha elections.

key_points: JP led the movement against Emergency and corruption in 1974-75
He gave the concept of Total Revolution (Sampoorna Kranti)
Janata Party won due to public anger against Emergency and atrocities
Unity of opposition parties against Congress boosted Janata Party

questions.solution:
Part (a): Jayaprakash Narayan, popularly known as JP, played a crucial role in Indian national politics, particularly during the 1970s. He led the Bihar Movement in 1974, demanding an end to corruption, unemployment, and misgovernance in Bihar. His movement soon spread nationally and he gave the call for Sampoorna Kranti or Total Revolution, demanding fundamental social, economic, and political transformation. JP united various opposition parties against the Congress government led by Indira Gandhi. When Emergency was declared in 1975, JP was arrested. After Emergency was lifted in 1977, JP played a key role in bringing together various opposition groups to form the Janata Party, which went on to defeat Indira Gandhi in the 1977 elections. His efforts symbolised the resilience of Indian democracy.

Part (b): The Janata Party's victory in 1977 was due to two main reasons. First, there was massive public anger and resentment against the excesses committed during the Emergency period (1975-77). Forced sterilisations, censorship of the press, arbitrary arrests of political opponents, and suspension of fundamental rights had deeply alienated ordinary citizens. Voters expressed their anger through the ballot box. Second, the unity of opposition parties was a decisive factor. Under JP's guidance, parties like the Congress (O), Jan Sangh, Socialists, and others merged to form the Janata Party, presenting a united front against the Congress. This prevented the splitting of anti-Congress votes and allowed the opposition to sweep the elections across northern India.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) जयप्रकाश नारायण ने 1974 में बिहार आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किया और 'सम्पूर्ण क्रांति' का आह्वान किया। उन्होंने विपक्षी दलों को एकजुट किया। आपातकाल में वे गिरफ्तार हुए। 1977 में जनता पार्टी बनाने में उनकी केंद्रीय भूमिका रही।
(b) 1977 में जनता पार्टी जीती क्योंकि: पहला, आपातकाल के दौरान जबरन नसबंदी, सेंसरशिप और मनमानी गिरफ्तारियों के कारण जनता में भारी आक्रोश था। दूसरा, विपक्षी दलों ने जनता पार्टी के रूप में एकजुट होकर कांग्रेस विरोधी मतों को एकत्रित किया।

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए अवतरण का अध्ययन कीजिए और दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :

sub_questions.solution: Regional diversity is the dominant form of diversity discussed in the passage. sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. The cartoon depicts the influence of the USA on the United Nations. The figure holding the UN logo represents the UN, while the 'WAR' monster on its other side represents the threat of military force. The message is that if the UN (diplomatic means) fails to achieve US objectives, then military force (war) will be used — illustrating how the USA exerts pressure on and through the UN to achieve its goals.

The message of the cartoon is that if the United Nations (the diplomatic 'right hand') fails to get what is desired, then the United States will use its military power (the 'WAR' monster as the 'left hand') to control the world. The cartoon satirises US hegemony and its use of the UN as a tool, with military force as the alternative.

Countries like China, Russia, India, and regional organisations like the EU have become significant global powers, reducing the unipolar dominance of the United States. The world has become multipolar, so the USA can no longer unilaterally dominate the UN or use it exclusively to serve its own interests.

(a) Explain any two contentious issues between China and India. Suggest any two measures to resolve these issues for greater cooperation.
OR
(b) "ASEAN took steps to establish an ASEAN community on the basis of its three pillars." Explain the importance of these three pillars.

key_points: Border disputes (McMahon Line, Aksai Chin, Arunachal Pradesh)
China's support to Pakistan and the issue of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir
Measures: dialogue through CBMs and joint border management mechanisms
ASEAN three pillars: Security Community, Economic Community, Socio-Cultural Community

questions.solution:
Part (a): Two major contentious issues between China and India are: First, the border dispute. China and India share a long and disputed border. China claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of South Tibet and occupies Aksai Chin, which India claims as part of Ladakh. The 1962 war was fought over these very issues and the border has remained unresolved. The Galwan Valley clash of 2020 shows this dispute is still active. Second, China's close strategic relationship with Pakistan. China has supported Pakistan militarily, diplomatically, and economically including building the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, which India strongly objects to. China's veto protection for Pakistan-based terror groups at the UN Security Council is another major irritant.

Two measures to resolve these issues are: First, strengthening Confidence Building Measures (CBMs) along the border, including regular meetings between military commanders, clear protocols for patrolling contested areas, and hotlines between the two governments to prevent escalation. Second, expanding bilateral trade and economic cooperation, as economic interdependence creates incentives for peaceful resolution of disputes. Both countries should revive high-level diplomatic dialogue and establish a permanent border management mechanism.

Part (b): ASEAN established its three-pillar community structure to achieve comprehensive regional integration. The three pillars are: First, the ASEAN Security Community, which aims to ensure that member states resolve disputes peacefully, maintain regional stability, and cooperate on non-traditional security threats like terrorism, piracy, and drug trafficking. This is important because regional peace is the prerequisite for all other development. Second, the ASEAN Economic Community, which aims to create a single market and production base within ASEAN by eliminating trade barriers, harmonising regulations, and facilitating the free flow of goods, services, capital, and skilled labour. This is vital because economic integration increases the prosperity of all member states. Third, the ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community, which fosters a sense of common identity and solidarity among the 600 million people of Southeast Asia through cultural exchanges, education cooperation, and social development initiatives. This pillar is important because lasting integration requires people-to-people bonds, not just government agreements.

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain any three security challenges faced by the newly independent countries of Asia and Africa after the Second World War.
OR
(b) Explain any three differences between the Non-traditional and Traditional notion of security.

key_points: Internal security threats from ethnic, religious, and regional conflicts
External threats from neighbouring countries and colonial powers
Traditional security focuses on military threats from states; non-traditional includes human security, environmental threats
Traditional uses military force; non-traditional requires cooperation and international institutions

questions.solution:
Part (a): Three security challenges faced by newly independent countries of Asia and Africa after World War II were: First, internal security threats arising from ethnic, religious, linguistic, and regional divisions within the newly created states. These newly independent countries often had artificial borders drawn by colonial powers that grouped together diverse communities with conflicting identities, leading to civil wars, ethnic cleansing, and separatist movements. Second, inter-state conflicts with neighbouring countries over territory, resources, and influence. Many new nations had unresolved border disputes with their neighbours, leading to wars. For example, India-Pakistan wars, Arab-Israeli conflicts, and various African border wars. Third, the challenge of building security institutions from scratch. These countries had to create armies, police forces, intelligence agencies, and legal systems while simultaneously dealing with active threats, with very limited resources and trained personnel.

Part (b): Three differences between traditional and non-traditional notions of security are: First, traditional security is primarily concerned with military threats to a nation-state from other nation-states. Non-traditional security recognises a much wider range of threats including terrorism, climate change, pandemics, poverty, and human rights violations that threaten not states but individual human beings. Second, traditional security focuses on the state as the primary referent object to be protected. Non-traditional security, influenced by the concept of Human Security, shifts the focus to the individual and communities as the ultimate referents. Third, traditional security relies primarily on military means — building armed forces, forming alliances, and deterrence — to address threats. Non-traditional security requires cooperation between states, international institutions, and civil society, as these threats cannot be solved by military force alone.

questions.text_english:
(a) "The foreign policy of Independent India has pursued the dream of a peaceful world." Support the statement with three suitable arguments.
OR
(b) "India played an important role in maintaining Afro-Asian Unity." Support the statement with three suitable examples.

key_points: India's policy of Non-Alignment kept it independent of Cold War blocs
India's role in UN peacekeeping missions worldwide
India's support for decolonisation and freedom movements
Bandung Conference 1955 and Panchsheel as examples of Afro-Asian unity

questions.solution:
Part (a): India's foreign policy has consistently pursued the dream of a peaceful world through the following three arguments. First, India adopted the policy of Non-Alignment under Nehru's leadership. By refusing to join either the American or Soviet military blocs during the Cold War, India maintained its independence and championed the cause of peace. India became a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in 1961, which united newly independent nations in rejecting Cold War militarism and advocating for peaceful coexistence. Second, India has been a major contributor to United Nations peacekeeping missions around the world, including in Korea, Congo, Gaza, and various African conflicts. By sending its armed forces to maintain peace in war-torn regions under UN command, India has demonstrated its commitment to international peace through multilateral cooperation. Third, India consistently supported the right to self-determination and decolonisation of nations in Asia and Africa. India opposed apartheid in South Africa, supported African freedom movements, and consistently voted in international forums against colonialism and racial discrimination, contributing to a more just and peaceful international order.

Part (b): India played a crucial role in maintaining Afro-Asian Unity through three examples. First, India was a key organiser of the Bandung Conference of 1955 in Indonesia, where 29 Asian and African nations met for the first time to assert their collective identity, promote solidarity, and oppose colonialism and racism. Nehru and other leaders articulated the Afro-Asian vision of peaceful coexistence. Second, India championed the Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) as a guiding framework for relations between Afro-Asian nations. These principles — mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality, and peaceful coexistence — became the ideological foundation for Afro-Asian solidarity. Third, India actively supported African nations in their struggles against colonialism and apartheid. India was one of the first countries to sever trade and diplomatic relations with apartheid South Africa, demonstrating concrete solidarity with African people and contributing to the maintenance of Afro-Asian unity in international forums.

questions.text_english:
(a) Describe any three major developments that took place in Indian politics in the last decade of the 20th century.
OR
(b) Describe any three recommendations of the Mandal Commission to solve the problems of the other backward classes.

key_points: Rise of coalition politics and fragmented mandate in 1989, 1991, 1996 elections
Economic liberalisation of 1991 under Manmohan Singh
Rise of BJP and hindutva politics, demolition of Babri Masjid 1992
Mandal Commission recommended 27% reservation for OBCs in government jobs and educational institutions
Recommendations included land redistribution and economic empowerment measures

questions.solution:
Part (a): Three major developments in Indian politics in the last decade of the 20th century (1990s) were: First, the rise of coalition politics and the end of single-party majority governments. The 1989 elections produced a hung parliament and V.P. Singh formed a minority government supported by the BJP and the Left. Subsequent elections in 1991, 1996, and 1998 also resulted in coalition arrangements. This decade marked the permanent shift from Congress dominance to multi-party coalition governments in India. Second, the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations in 1990 under V.P. Singh's government, providing 27% reservation to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in central government jobs. This led to massive nationwide protests and counter-protests, and fundamentally transformed the social and political landscape by mobilising OBC communities as a major political force. Third, the destruction of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya on 6 December 1992 and the subsequent communal riots were a watershed event. It led to the rise of Hindutva politics, brought the BJP to national prominence, and created a major fault line in Indian society and politics that continued to shape elections throughout the decade.

Part (b): Three major recommendations of the Mandal Commission (1980) to solve the problems of Other Backward Classes were: First, the Commission recommended 27% reservation for OBCs in central government jobs and public sector undertakings, in addition to the existing 22.5% for Scheduled Castes and Tribes, bringing the total reservation to 49.5%. This was the most significant recommendation aimed at giving OBCs fair representation in government employment. Second, the Commission recommended 27% reservation for OBCs in admissions to central government educational institutions and universities. This was aimed at improving access to higher education for OBC communities who had historically been denied equal educational opportunities. Third, the Commission recommended a programme of land reforms and economic measures to improve the material condition of OBCs, including redistribution of surplus land to landless OBC families and special development programmes targeting OBC-dominated villages and communities, recognising that political representation alone was insufficient without economic empowerment.
